record.original_question: Determine what criteria decide whether a positive series sum a_n converges or diverges. Equivalently, is there a universal algorithmic convergence test, or any general structural pattern, that characterizes convergence versus divergence for arbitrary positive series?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. What decides if a positive series is convergent or divergent? Is there any universal convergence test? Is there any pattern in convergence?
Problem 2. Find an algorithm to determine whether a positive series is convergent or not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider positive real-valued sequences $(a_n)_{n\ge 1}$ with $a_n>0$, and the associated series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n$. A "convergence test" is, informally, a rule or algorithm that takes as input a description of the sequence $(a_n)$ and outputs either "convergent" or "divergent" in agreement with the actual behavior of $\sum a_n$.

Address the following:

(a) Does there exist a universal convergence test for positive series? More precisely, does there exist a single criterion (e.g. of the form: the convergence of $\sum a_n$ is equivalent to the convergence/divergence of some auxiliary explicitly constructible series, or to a comparison with a fixed scale of sequences) that decides convergence versus divergence for every positive series $\sum a_n$?

(b) Equivalently, exhibit an algorithm which, given an arbitrary positive sequence $(a_n)$ (presented in some reasonable computational form), decides whether $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n$ converges, or prove that no such algorithm exists.

(c) Identify any general structural pattern (a totally ordered scale of "rates of convergence/divergence", a hierarchy of comparison series, etc.) which characterizes the boundary between convergent and divergent positive series.
artifact.status_search_result: It is a classical theorem of Abel and Du Bois-Reymond that no universal convergence test exists for positive series: for any convergent positive series one can construct a convergent series that converges arbitrarily more slowly, and similarly for divergence. Hence there is no totally ordered scale of comparison series and no single criterion characterizing convergence of all positive series. This negative result has been known since the 19th century, and recent work continues to extend specific tests, but the universal-test question itself is settled in the negative.

status_evidence.snippet: Du Bois-Reymond established classical results showing no universal scale of comparison exists for series convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Classical theorem of Abel/Du Bois-Reymond rules out a universal convergence test for positive series.

status_evidence.title: A new test for convergence of positive series (arXiv:2104.04622)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper proposes a new convergence test for positive series, extending the existing collection of partial tests.
status_evidence.claim: Research continues on individual tests, consistent with the absence of a single universal test.
